- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid missing reversal.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–3% from forecast for 2–3 days.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is near recent mean, model often drifts toward extremes; apply mean-reversion bias: pull forecast toward 10–15% of recent 7-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; reduce first 3–5 forecast points by 1–3% to align with true volatility.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated “bullish → bearish” swings, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of delay in price drop forecasts to match sentiment reversal.
